newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece interested to invest in Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Greece interested to invest in Bulgaria.

text.p: Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said on Tuesday Athens wanted closer relations with neighbouring Bulgaria and that Greek business were eager to invest once a new government emerged from Saturday's elections.

"We believe that the Bulgarian economy has very good growth prospects and we encourage Greek investments," Pangalos told reporters after talks with visiting interim Bulgarian Foreign Minister Stoyan Stalev.

He said the state Greek Telecommunications Organisation (OTE) was planning to participate as an investor in the upcoming privatisation of the Bulgarian telecoms company and that there was interest to improve road and rail links from the northern city of Salonika to Sofia.
Stalev said one of the priorities of the new Bulgarian government should be to make the country attractive to foreign investors with a stable business climate.
"Bulgaria is on its way out of the acute economic crisis it went through last year," Stalev said.
Pangalos and Stalev had lunch with a group of top Greek bussinessmen in the telecommunications, construction and banking sectors.

Pangalos said the final details on the construction of a pipeline to bring Russian crude oil through Bulgaria to Greece had been ironed out and expected a final agreement would be reached by Bulgaria's new government.
He also said Greece backed Bulgaria's request to be become a European Union and NATO member and that the cost of visas of Bulgarians visiting Greece would be cut from 50,000 lev to 30,000 ($20).
